project.name: example-project
project.intent: Classify runtime readiness faults and return exact recovery actions while preserving source, schema, tool, and worker identity.

evidence.observation: The synthetic valid control passes every declared source, schema, tool, and worker check.
The fixture marks its checkout dirty so compilation must refuse before producing a draft.
The fault fixture refuses a participant when the declared linker cannot be opened.
The fault fixture refuses a participant when its temporary directory is not writable.
The fault fixture refuses an incomplete native build environment.
No sealed and verdict-only fault population is included in this public example.
evidence.limitation: The disclosed fixture can test development behavior but cannot support a promotion decision.

opportunity.intended_outcome: Return the expected closed diagnosis and corrective action for more runtime faults without introducing false-ready or false-fault results.
opportunity.quantitative_primary: Count of fixture cases receiving the exact expected readiness classification and recovery contract.
opportunity.inference_scope: The result applies only to the disclosed synthetic cases and toolchain contract. It makes no claim about other faults, platforms, or promotion readiness.

anti_goodhart.capability_deletion: The valid control must remain ready and every identity check remains present, so deleting checks or always refusing cannot improve the primary outcome.
anti_goodhart.workload_narrowing: The adapter executes the complete case manifest and rejects missing, duplicated, or reordered cases.
anti_goodhart.cost_displacement: Diagnostic latency and external probe count are protected objectives, and setup work remains inside the measured process.
anti_goodhart.test_weakening: Fixtures, expected outcomes, and the adapter are frozen outside the candidate mutation allowlist.
anti_goodhart.self_certification: The external adapter derives verdicts from process output and the frozen oracle; candidate-authored success labels are ignored.

native_observables: Structured readiness result and per-check status
Stable failure code and corrective action
invariants: Successful checks contain no stale failure metadata
Source, schema, tool, and worker identities remain explicit
negative_controls: Candidate that reports a missing authority as ready
Invalid schema and missing tool environments
candidate_scope: Contract tests for failed and successful check rows

fixtures.oracle: Exact expected overall state, failed check, failure code, and corrective action.
fixtures.limitation: The cases are disclosed to candidate code; repeated blocks are deterministic replays, not independent population samples.
Unavailable in this public example and therefore ineligible for promotion evidence.

environment_requirements.required_behavior: Build the exact participant source under the declared toolchain.
Link participant build products using the declared search paths.
Provide a fresh writable temporary directory to build subprocesses.
Bind compiler, include, library, system root, path, temporary directory, and child-process inheritance before admission.

uncertainties: The disclosed matrix does not establish behavior on unseen fault classes.
The complete native child-process environment is intentionally unavailable.
The synthetic checkout is marked dirty and cannot compile into a campaign draft.
resource_costs: Each participant requires a build unless an independently verified source-bound artifact is available.
A paired calibration and research series executes every matrix twice per block.
Disclosed workspace evidence supports development decisions but not sealed promotion.
opportunity.adapter_requirement: Run the exact participant CLI against the bound fixture matrix, retain per-case receipts, and emit every admitted objective without self-certified verdicts.
